pageCache.pageTitle: Private Prep School in West London - Clifton Lodge School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Clifton Lodge School
Everything we do is driven by helping your child to be their best. We are Clifton Lodge, a small prep school based in Ealing, caring for children aged 4 to 11 years old. we use the word small on purpose – we see 'small' as our biggest advantage; our size allows us to provide an environment which makes our children feel safe, secure, comfortable and at home. We see that, together with our Christian ethos as being instrumental to laying great foundations for personal wellbeing, the ability to thrive, which in turn leads to achievement. Children are taught by a team of dedicated staff who pull out all the stops to ensure each child’s needs are catered to. But don’t just take our word for it. - The Independent Schools’ Inspectorate awarded the school their highest accolade of double “Excellent” in both the academic and personal development of the children. - Our parents who have described Clifton Lodge as “the best possible learning environment” and a school which “builds confidence” and “pushes academically.” Come along to meet the Clifton Lodge family to see for yourself how we can help your child be their best.
We prepare for
ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE
We encourage a growth mindset which will develop children’s resilience and curiosity, cultivating skills for the future. Our school motto, 'Optime' inspires all at Clifton Lodge to achieve excellence in everything we do.
We champion
PUPIL WELLBEING
We provide a small, family environment which fosters a sense of belonging and allows our children to feel happy, confident and secure. Wellbeing and kindness are at the centre of our educational approach. We ensure that all our children feel valued, listened to and included at school.
We prepare for
11+ ENTRANCE EXAMS
Our pupils are supported and prepared for 11+ entry to highly selective senior schools. We assist our parents with senior school choices and provide insight into how we help each child attain the best possible option for their future learning.
Join our next Open Event
Mr Belsito joined Clifton Lodge School in September 2022. He started his teaching career at our school and was delighted to return many years later as Head. He has considerable experience and knowledge of the local area and schools through his senior roles in both state and independent schools in Ealing.
"Clifton Lodge has a unique feel that everybody notices when they walk through the front door."
- Michael Belsito, Headmaster
FACILITIES & LOCATION
An environment that makes all feel welcome
Our school is located in an extended double-fronted Victorian home in Ealing, close to the centre and only 10 minutes walk from Ealing Broadway Station (Elizabeth Line, Central and District Lines). There is ample parking (payment by phone or by meter) directly across the road, opposite the school. The school provides a wonderful range of facilities to enhance pupils’ learning. Our classrooms are bright and fully equipped, including a science lab and art studio. A large playground with a canopied area gives pupils much needed space for play, events, assemblies and PE. In addition we are sited opposite Walpole Park which we regularly use for outdoor learning.
Learn about the latest news
Our pupils are eager to share their achievements and we celebrate their successes together with trips, concerts, sporting fixtures, events and the many other exciting activities happening year round to support our pupils’ learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our School Ethos and Aims - Clifton Lodge School
pageCache.text:
School Ethos & Aims
We develop young people who are self-assured, self-driven, and fully prepared for the next chapter of their adventure, whether it is moving on to senior school, moving across the world, or moving up in our school. Our values and goals are essential for creating a positive and productive learning environment for pupils. They provide a framework for the school's culture, curriculum, policies, and help to create a learning environment that fosters academic and personal growth for its pupils. The Clifton Lodge School Virtues of: Love, Integrity, Justice, Wisdom, Fortitude and Self-Control underpin our approach which encourages all our children to be their best.
To nurture each child to be their best.
We provide a small, family environment which fosters a sense of belonging and allows our children to feel happy, confident and secure.
We encourage a growth mindset which will develop children’s resilience and curiosity, cultivating skills for the future.
We offer a personalised learning journey for our children, building on their individual strengths from whatever their starting points.
We fulfil our school motto “Optime” by aspiring to excellence in all that we do.
Clifton Lodge is an inclusive, friendly, family-feel school which nurtures excellence in a culture that promotes and celebrates wellbeing as well as academic attainment. Our pupils are challenged and encouraged to express themselves to develop their character, resilience and empathy. But what makes life at Clifton Lodge truly special is our multicultural, diverse, global community, which embraces a wide variety of faiths, languages and traditions. We celebrate all of our families and staff backgrounds.
Join us for an Open Day
Join us for an Open Day or book a private tour during the week so you can experience the school in action. We will be delighted to discuss your child's needs in detail and show you how they can benefit from a Clifton Lodge School education.
Providing a safe and caring environment for our pupils to thrive.
We want children to feel safe, happy and enjoy coming to school.
Instilling a love of learning in all our pupils, building curiosity about what they do not yet know.
Nurturing pupils' values, integrity, and empathy, while equipping them with the skills to become responsible and compassionate members of society.
‘Optime’, our school motto means ‘Try always to do your best’. This combined with our School Virtues: Love, Integrity, Self-Control, Wisdom, Fortitude & Justice, inspires our pupils to aim high and tackle challenges with a growth mindset.
Clifton Lodge School

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative & Performing Arts - Art, Music & Drama at Clifton Lodge
pageCache.text:
Creative Arts & Music
Creative Arts are essential to the curriculum
Drama, Art and Music flourish at Clifton Lodge and play a significant role in the curriculum and after-school clubs. Our creative teachers are constantly seeking new ideas to support our pupils' creative growth while inspiring them to discover and pursue their artistic passions. Many children take individual instrument lessons, join the choir or have LAMDA or Ballet lessons. Every pupil from Reception to Year 6 performs in at least one event each year in front of other pupils and their parents. Pupils are given the chance to develop their talents and perform in front of an audience in a supportive environment.
Art
Music
School Choir
Drama
Pupils participate in real art experiences
We inspire a passion for art among our pupils from Reception to Year 6. We create an environment that encourages creativity and independence so that children have the courage to share their works of art. During lessons, pupils are encouraged to experiment with various media and consider other artists' works from a historical and international perspective. We constantly change the projects children work on to ensure that they are fresh and relevant to the world around us.
Music is an integral part of our well-rounded education
Our pupils in all school stages benefit from lessons with our expert Music Teacher each week. In addition to building creativity and teamwork, music classes also allow our pupils to grow in confidence and self-esteem. Alongside scheduled music lessons, we have a thriving choir in Prep and Pre-Prep. Both give the opportunity to perform at events throughout the year in front of their parents and in the local community. All our year groups also regularly participate in singing at events and can enjoy individual piano or guitar lessons with our expert peri teachers.
We have a thriving main school choir at Clifton Lodge
Pupils from Year 3 can audition to be part of the choir at the start of the academic year. Being part of the choir requires a commitment to learn the songs, attend rehearsals twice a week at lunchtime, and all the performances. The choir cover a wide ranging repertoire of songs and styles from classical, baroque, folk, pop, blues to name a few. The children enjoy singing in three part harmonies as well as in unison and acapella. They perform at many of the school events and festivals throughout the year such as Harvest and Remembrance assemblies, the Christmas carol concert, the Spring concert and Speech day. Alongside the choir, our school band performs regularly at events with pupils encouraged to join and play instruments including keyboards & percussion to accompany the choir.
Drama lessons are part of our core curriculum
Pupils have numerous opportunities to take part in events and productions throughout the year which showcase their talents in music and drama. In addition, we regularly invite ‘Perform’ into school to hold drama workshops with our Lower School pupils. Older pupils can take part in our annual drama production, there are opportunities both on stage and behind the scenes to get involved. In addition, we have an excellent LAMDA (speech & drama) Teacher. Pupils are taught in small groups and take external LAMDA examinations. We also have Ballet Lessons from Early Years to Year 4 with our teacher, Anna Davydova.
Clifton Lodge School

pageCache.pageTitle: Leavers' Results & Destinations - Clifton Lodge School
pageCache.text:
Leavers' Destinations
We support each parent in the process of selecting the right senior school for their child
We are very experienced in the process of choosing suitable senior schools for each pupil and are aware that every child has specific abilities, individual talents and requirements. Our Head not only knows our pupils well but also has connections with each senior school, understanding their ethos and entrance conditions to assist parents with this sometimes daunting task.
Careers Guidance
We’re here to support our students and make sure they know about all the options open to them. We focus on the future and provide our students with meaningful career-related opportunities and activities throughout their time with us. As part of Blenheim Schools, we have access to qualified careers professional pathways, through Careers Advisory Lead, Kelly Guthery (RCDP Level 7). If you have any questions about careers, or if you would like more information about our careers programme, please contact us at the school or to speak with Kelly please email Kelly.Guthery@ofgl.co.uk.
Preparing pupils for their next steps
As a prep school, we prepare and support our pupils with entrance to their preferred 11+ senior schools. Historically the most popular schools for boys leaving Clifton Lodge have been Merchant Taylors’ School, City of London Boys’ School, Hampton, The John Lyon School and St Benedict’s. Girls leaving us in Year 6 have gained places at Notting Hill & Ealing High School, St Augustine’s Priory, St Benedict’s, Latymer Upper School, Godolphin & Latymer & Putney High.
Join us for an Open Day
We have a variety of ways for you to experience what our school has to offer. We would be delighted to invite you to our wonderful school and share with you what makes Clifton Lodge School the best educational start you can give your child.

Open Days & Visits
Learn more about the benefits of a Clifton Lodge education
We would like to extend a warm welcome to you at Clifton Lodge and our admissions team will be delighted to assist you throughout the process. You can experience what our school has to offer in a number of ways. Families often visit us on one of our popular Saturday open days when we offer informal tours led by some of our older pupils. We are also delighted to arrange private tours during the school day which enable parents to see the school in action and have a more in-depth conversation about their child's needs. Book one of our Private Tours or Open Mornings below.

Directions
Our next Open Day
Families often first visit us on one of our popular Saturday open days when we offer informal tours led by some of our older pupils. Teaching staff are on hand in each classroom to discuss the curriculum and individual parent enquiries. After a tour, visitors are encouraged to meet our Leadership Team and Inclusion Manager and enjoy refreshments. Open Days start at 10am and finish at noon and we welcome parents and children to join us. Our admissions team are always on hand to discuss your child’s education and support you throughout the process. Please feel free to contact us to learn more about our welcoming environment, small classes and high-quality teaching tailored to your child’s individual needs.
Enjoy a private tour tailored to you
Come and experience what our school has to offer
We can arrange private tours during the school day – please contact our Admissions Registrar or complete the form below to book a tour. We firmly believe that education is about individuals so we also encourage prospective parents to visit on a normal school day; this allows parents to have individual discussions with the Head so that they can address their own questions and concerns. Parents also have the opportunity to see the classes in action, with children going about their daily lessons and activities. Whether an open day is not convenient or, having visited the school once, you wish to see the school on a normal day, we would be delighted to arrange a tour to suit you.

Sport & Competition
Our pupils enjoy a healthy and active lifestyle
We are well aware of the importance of regular exercise for maintaining our physical and mental wellbeing, as well as embedding healthy routines early in life. It is also crucial for our school's youngest pupils to participate in regular PE and sport activities to support their growth and motor skills. We are fortunate to benefit from our partnership with Ealing Trailfinders Rugby Club who provide all our sports provision onsite and offsite, ensuring that our pupils are given expert tuition and have the use of the professional facilities at the Rugby Club each week.
A variety of Sports & Activities
Our sports provision is taught by professionals, in partnership with Ealing Trailfinders Rugby Club. Lessons are taught each week onsite and offsite at Trailfinders sports ground. On Fridays, all pupils from Year 3 to 6 have an afternoon of sports at Trailfinders. The club prides itself on the excellence of its sporting facilities set in 20 acres of landscaped grounds. The facilities include: • 2 full size 3G all weather rugby pitches and grandstand - floodlit • 2 grass rugby pitches • Minis rugby pitch • Cricket pitch, pavilion, score box, sight screens and nets • 4 floodlit tennis courts/netball courts - floodlit • 3G all weather 5/7- a-side football/training pitch - floodlit • 3 softball squares There are different focused sports each term, including football, rugby, netball, rounders, cricket and athletics, culminating in our whole school annual sports day. Years 1 & 2 have swimming lessons on Friday afternoons at a local pool. We participate in regular sports fixtures against local schools and celebrate our pupil's sporting achievements in and out of school.
Our sports programme helps pupils to develop their physical skills
Clifton Lodge School

A vibrant extra-curricular programme to broaden experiences
At Clifton Lodge School, we think education should give your child the chance to discover and explore new abilities as well as to foster curiosity about the world and the people in it. There is an activity for every child whether they are interested in science, drama, ballet, chess, music and performance, digital and creative arts, sport, or cookery.

Reaching new heights
Trips and visits should be a part of every child's education since they reinforce their learning experience. Trips provide first-hand memories that stay with them for much longer than reading about it in a book or doing research online. To enhance our pupils' education, our teachers at Clifton Lodge organise termly day trips. We provide a wide range of excursions across the school, including residential trips that promote character development and academic enrichment. Clifton Lodge school trips are a crucial component of our curriculum and educational philosophy to expand learning outside of the classroom and help pupils acquire important life skills.

After School Care
After-school Care is available each afternoon during term-time until 6pm (excluding the last day of each term). Our dedicated staff provide a range of activities for all ages from 3.30-6pm each day. There is a charge for After-School Care. Please contact us for more details.

High Fliers runs at Clifton Lodge Prep School in Ealing for children aged 3-11, we are open during the school holidays. We have a huge range of fun and engaging activities planned for your children, in a nurturing and warm environment. Our staff are experienced and qualified and we offer specialist workshops to give your children a fantastic experience. Visit the High Fliers website for more information:

11+ Preparation
We excel at preparing pupils for the 11+ examinations
Preparation for the 11+ begins in Year 1 and is embedded throughout subsequent years. We ensure that by the time our pupils take their exams in Year 6 they are confident and well-prepared. Pupils are instructed on how to use and apply their knowledge in both exam papers and interviews. Additionally, pupils sit the Progress Test in English (PTE), the Progress Test in Maths (PTM) and the Cognitive Abilities Test (CAT4) from Year 1 onwards on an annual basis. We aim to support each individual child throughout the process, with their wellbeing placed at the heart to both reduce stress levels and ensure success. We are very proud that many of our Year 6 pupils excel at 11+ and receive offers from a range of sought-after senior schools.

pageCache.text:
Leavers' Destinations
We support each parent in the process of selecting the right senior school for their child
We are very experienced in the process of choosing suitable senior schools for each pupil and are aware that every child has specific abilities, individual talents and requirements. Our Head not only knows our pupils well but also has connections with each senior school, understanding their ethos and entrance conditions to assist parents with this sometimes daunting task.
Careers Guidance
We’re here to support our students and make sure they know about all the options open to them. We focus on the future and provide our students with meaningful career-related opportunities and activities throughout their time with us. As part of Blenheim Schools, we have access to qualified careers professional pathways, through Careers Advisory Lead, Kelly Guthery (RCDP Level 7). If you have any questions about careers, or if you would like more information about our careers programme, please contact us at the school or to speak with Kelly please email Kelly.Guthery@ofgl.co.uk.
Preparing pupils for their next steps
As a prep school, we prepare and support our pupils with entrance to their preferred 11+ senior schools. Historically the most popular schools for boys leaving Clifton Lodge have been Merchant Taylors’ School, City of London Boys’ School, Hampton, The John Lyon School and St Benedict’s. Girls leaving us in Year 6 have gained places at Notting Hill & Ealing High School, St Augustine’s Priory, St Benedict’s, Latymer Upper School, Godolphin & Latymer & Putney High.
Join us for an Open Day
We have a variety of ways for you to experience what our school has to offer. We would be delighted to invite you to our wonderful school and share with you what makes Clifton Lodge School the best educational start you can give your child.

pageCache.pageTitle: Private Pre-Prep in Ealing - Clifton Lodge School
pageCache.text:
Pre-Prep School
An enriched, dynamic curriculum
Key Stage 1 is an important bridge in a child’s development as they are putting into practice all the skills and foundational knowledge that they have gained in EYFS and building upon them. Years 1 and 2 are situated in large bright rooms on the upper ground floor which incorporates them into the more formal learning atmosphere in the main building whilst also retaining the space required for children of this age.
Teaching children confidence and independent thinking
Years 1 and 2 signal the beginning of National Curriculum expectations and standardised testing to enable progress tracking. The curriculum is taught in separate subjects while children gain confidence and independence in their learning and abilities. Phonics and reading continue to be essential with most children finishing the phonics scheme by the end of Year 2. Maths and English are key and form the beginning of each day’s timetable. The Core Knowledge Curriculum for Science, Music, Art, History and Geography is introduced in this Key Stage and continues throughout the school. Other subjects taught by the class teacher include Computing, Drama, Religious Studies, Reasoning and PSHE. Additional specialised teaching begins in Year 1 in the Art room. Year 1 & 2 pupils also go swimming on a Friday afternoon.
Join us for an Open Day
We have a variety of ways for you to experience what our school has to offer. We encourage visits during the day so that you can see our school in action and will be able to discuss your child's needs in more detail.
A broad curriculum to stimulate and challenge pupils
In the pre-prep stage, the curriculum is designed to encourage children to develop a love for learning while also building their social, emotional, and physical skills. The curriculum is designed to provide a foundation for future learning and development. The school aims to provide a nurturing and stimulating environment where children can learn, grow, and thrive.
Having grasped basics in French in Reception, children in Key Stage 1 will progress to learn topic vocabulary and increase their confidence in spoken French through repetition, games and songs. Written work is limited at this stage as oral comprehension and an accurate accent are more important to ensure understanding moving forward.
Sport is taught once a week in the safety of our main playground by specially trained coaches from Ealing Trailfinders. Skills and team games are taught which build upon and extend those gained in EYFS. The sporting highlight of the year is the School Sports Day held in June which everyone takes part in to represent their House. Every Friday afternoon Years 1 and 2 go swimming at a local swimming pool. They are assessed in their first lesson of the academic year and placed in ability groups taught by Swimming Teachers. Assessments are carried out at the end of each term culminating in a final one at the end of the year after which children will receive Swimming badges and certificates.
Years 1 and 2 are taught Music once a week by the Music teacher which involves learning about rhythm, playing with sound, using their voice, responding to music and playing percussion and the tin whistle. Alongside these aspects of Music, the children will be learning how to look out for these musical elements in famous works whilst also familiarising themselves with key composers. Once a week there is a Key Stage 1 choir lesson which every child in Years 1 & 2 takes part in. There are also visiting peripatetic teachers to individually teach piano and guitar.
Art is taught by the Art teacher once a week. Children will learn about the elements of Art such as colour, line, shape and texture alongside types of Art, studying well known pieces and gaining familiarity with famous artists. They will have the opportunity to put this learning into practise in each unit either in 2D or 3D form.
EXTRA-CURRICULAR, CLUBS & TRIPS
Music
Art
Our pupils excel beyond the classroom
Our pupils in Years 1 & 2 have a trip or workshop each term. With a wealth of museums, theatres and locations to visit, our trips are carefully planned to support and extend the classroom learning, often including tailored workshops. There are two clubs a week run by the teachers in Key Stage 1 which parents may sign children up to. Ballet Lessons with our Ballet Teacher who visits the school each Wednesday are available at an extra cost. Clubs change each term and are run after school until 4.45pm. After school care is available each day until 6pm.

pageCache.pageTitle: Private Prep School in Ealing - Clifton Lodge School
pageCache.text:
Prep School
Growing minds, building futures
Pupils in Years 3 to 6 are encouraged to become more independent learners and assume more responsibility for their daily tasks. We put a lot of emphasis on problem-solving and practical learning, and encouraging the pupils to be curious and explore subjects in order to understand them better. There are high expectations of work, independence, presentation and organisation for all our children in Key Stage 2. Having Maths and English Specialists as the Year 5 and 6 form teachers ensures continuity for the last two years and enables the teachers to really know the children’s ability in these subjects which form the basis of the 11+. Year 5 sit weekly practice tests from the February half term and throughout the Autumn term of Year 6. In the Autumn term of Year 6 children have lessons on interview skills followed by practice interviews with either the Head or Deputy Head. Both Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning are taught in class through tests and applied practice.
Join us for an Open Day
We have a variety of ways for you to experience what our school has to offer. We encourage visits during the day so that you can see our school in action and will be able to discuss your child's needs in more detail.
A broad curriculum to stimulate and challenge pupils
There are high expectations of work, independence, presentation and organisation for children in Key Stage 2. Standardised testing continues and progress is tracked which contributes towards scholarships offers within school. Tracking also helps inform conversations with parents about future schools. Each day begins with Maths and English followed by the other subjects taught by class teachers (Geography, History, Religious Studies, Reasoning, Computing, PSHE and Drama).
Students in Key Stage 2 have one French lesson per week where they will develop their oral comprehension skills and learn about grammar and written French. They will revisit previously learnt topics to learn spellings and be able to communicate accurately in written form, drawing on their understanding of speaking and grammar rules.
At Clifton Lodge we appreciate the importance of good, motivating Sports tuition for health, teamwork and achievement. Sport is played on two days each week with additional matches and competitions throughout the year. One lesson is held on-site in the main playground and on Friday afternoons Key Stage 2 travel to Ealing Trailfinders Sports Ground. All our Sport is taught by specially trained coaches from Ealing Trailfinders. We focus on skills and team games through football, tag rugby, hockey, netball, cricket and rounders. The sporting highlight of the year is the School Sports Day held in June which everyone takes part in to represent their House.
Years 3-6 are taught Music once a week by the Music teacher. In singing, pupils develop their expression and awareness of phrases and try out singing in parts. Pupils also look at how composers employ the musical elements and recreate these effects, contributing their own ideas. In instrumental work, they further develop their understanding and application of music notation and rhythms when learning more extensive tin whistle pieces. Children in Key Stage 2 have the opportunity to audition for the School Choir. The Clifton Lodge School Choir is very highly regarded and performs at all the public assemblies and Speech Day; being a member of it is a prestigious position and requires commitment to attend all events and rehearsals. There are also visiting peripatetic teachers to individually teach piano and guitar.
Key Stage 2 pupils have one Art lesson a week with the specialist Art teacher. They will build on their knowledge and skills in the elements of art such as line, symmetry and form, study different types of Art such as architecture, embroidery and needlework and look at country specific Art. In Key Stage 2 they will have the opportunity to study well known pieces and gain familiarity with famous artists. At the end of each unit the pupils will put this learning into practise in either 2D or 3D form.
Science specialist teaching starts in Year 3 in our dedicated Science Lab. Chemistry, Biology and Physics are all covered in topics such as Cycles in Nature, Simple Machines, The Human Body, Light and Optics, Matter and Change. The fully equipped Science lab enables practical experiments within lessons which bring to life the theory studied.
EXTRA-CURRICULAR, CLUBS & TRIPS
Music
Art
Learning outside of the classroom
Key Stage 2 children have the opportunity to take a day trip each term. With a wealth of museums, theatres and locations to visit, our trips are carefully planned to support and extend classroom learning, often including tailored workshops. There is also a residential trip each year open to Key Stage 2. Clubs are run after school by teachers from Monday to Thursday. They draw on the interests and talents of our teachers with some external clubs at an additional cost. Clubs change each term and are run after school until 5.15pm.
Preparing pupils for the future
Having Maths and English Specialists as the Year 5 and 6 form teachers ensures continuity for the last two years and enables the teachers to really know the children’s ability in these subjects which form the basis of the 11+. Year 5 sit weekly practice tests from the February half term and throughout the Autumn term of Year 6. In the Autumn term of Year 6 children have lessons on interview skills followed by practice interviews with either the Head or Deputy Head. Both Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning is taught in class through tests and applied practice at certain question types.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reception - Private School In Ealing - Clifton Lodge
pageCache.text:
Reception Class
The first big step on their academic journey
In our welcoming and vibrant Reception class, pupils advance their way through the EYFS expectations. Our own expectations are high, daily individual reading aloud, and children often attain levels of achievement beyond what is normally expected at this age. Our pupils enjoy the challenges and are encouraged to try their best, building confidence and an early love of learning. Art and craft are focussed around the topics being studied throughout the year, developing the children’s imaginations and creative flair.
Join us for an Open Day
We have a variety of ways for you to experience what our school has to offer. We encourage visits during the day so that you can see our school in action and will be able to discuss your child's needs in more detail.
Pupils are encouraged to try their best
In Reception, the emphasis is on play-based learning and exploration, with a focus on developing children's social, emotional, and communication skills. The curriculum is designed to be flexible, with activities and learning opportunities tailored to each child's individual needs and interests. Throughout the year, teachers will assess children's progress and development against the Early Learning Goals (ELGs), which are the expectations for the end of Reception. Our Reception children in 2024 achieved 93% Good Level of Development (GLD). Nationally 67% of children achieved a good level of development.
Reception children receive French lessons once a week with a specialist teacher. The language is introduced through learning to speak French words and phrases via games and songs.
Sport is taught once a week in the safety of our main playground by specially trained coaches from Ealing Trailfinders. Skills and team games are taught, providing exercise, fun and the opportunity to meet and exceed the goals for Physical Activity in the EYFS expectations. The sporting highlight of the year is the School Sports Day held in June which everyone takes part in to represent their House.
Pupils in Reception enjoy a Music lesson taught by our specialist teacher every week. The youngest children learn to engage with music through song, movement and sensory activities. As their skills develop, they learn about the musical elements, responding to music through movement, playing percussion instruments and singing. There is also a visiting peripatetic teacher to individually teach piano.
Our pupils in Reception have a wonderful opportunity to experience Forest School in our local Lammas Park. A specially trained teacher takes them for weekly sessions where they are able to explore their environment and learn more about it in focused activities.
EXTRA-CURRICULAR, CLUBS & TRIPS
Music
Forest School
Outside the classroom
Reception pupils enjoy a school trip each term, our trips are carefully planned to support and expand classroom topics and often involve participating in tailored workshops. There are two extra-curricular clubs a week run by the EYFS staff which pupils can be signed up to. Ballet Lessons with our Ballet Teacher who visits the school each Wednesday are available at an extra cost. Clubs change each term and are run after school until 4.15pm. After school care is available each day until 6pm.
